title: Google Overhauls AI Leadership as Hassabis Steps Back and Jeff Dean Exits After 27 Years
excerpt: DeepMind's Nobel Prize-winning CEO becomes Alphabet's chief scientist while four veteran engineers leave to co-found Discovery Loop, deepening concerns about Google's AI talent drain.
body:
• Demis Hassabis is stepping down as CEO of Google DeepMind to become chairman of DeepMind and Alphabet's newly created chief scientist, while Koray Kavukcuoglu takes over day-to-day operations as senior vice president.
  • Jeff Dean, Google's chief scientist and its 30th employee, is leaving after 27 years to co-found Discovery Loop, a public benefit startup focused on automating scientific research, alongside veterans Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals, and Quoc Le.
  • The shakeup follows a wave of high-profile departures, including transformer co-author Noam Shazeer to OpenAI and AlphaFold Nobel co-winner John Jumper to Anthropic, raising questions about Google's ability to retain top AI talent.
  • Alphabet shares fell 4% on the news as investors weigh the company's delayed release of Gemini 3.5 Pro and its third-place position behind OpenAI and Anthropic in frontier AI benchmarks.

Hassabis Shifts to 'Big Picture' Role

Google parent Alphabet announced a sweeping overhaul of its AI leadership on Wednesday, with Nobel Prize-winning scientist Demis Hassabis stepping down as chief executive of Google DeepMind to take on a newly created role as Alphabet's chief scientist and DeepMind's chairman.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=agj_SncIqH8

Hassabis, who founded DeepMind in 2010 and sold it to Google for £400 million in 2014, said in a staff memo that he wanted to focus on shaping the trajectory of artificial general intelligence rather than managing day-to-day operations.

"I've decided that now is the right time for me to hand over my day-to-day operational responsibilities at Google DeepMind, so I have the time and space to focus on the big picture and help influence what is to come."

— Demis Hassabis, in a memo to DeepMind staff

Koray Kavukcuoglu, DeepMind's chief technology officer, will assume responsibility for all AI-model development. He will hold the title of senior vice president rather than CEO, reflecting a structural change in how the division reports within Alphabet. Kavukcuoglu will also serve as Alphabet's chief AI architect. Hassabis will remain CEO of Isomorphic Labs, Google's AI-driven drug discovery subsidiary.

Dean Departs After 27 Years

The more startling development may be the departure of Jeff Dean, Google's chief scientist and one of the most decorated engineers in Silicon Valley. Dean, who joined Google as its 30th employee in 1999, is leaving to co-found Discovery Loop, a public benefit corporation focused on automating breakthroughs in machine learning, science, and engineering.

He is taking three other Google luminaries with him: Sanjay Ghemawat, who co-designed many of Google's foundational infrastructure systems; Oriol Vinyals, a key architect behind Gemini; and Quoc Le, a pioneer in automated machine learning. Google confirmed it will invest in Discovery Loop, according to The Times of London.

Their departures follow a string of exits that have depleted Google's AI bench. In June, transformer architecture co-author Noam Shazeer left for OpenAI, and John Jumper—who shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Hassabis for work on the protein-folding system AlphaFold—joined Anthropic. Two other DeepMind researchers, Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel, also left that month.

A Competitive Crisis

The leadership changes arrive at a particularly fraught moment for Google's AI ambitions. The company's flagship Gemini 3.5 Pro model remains unreleased despite a planned June launch, and its existing models have generally trailed those of OpenAI and Anthropic on widely used benchmark tests.

Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai acknowledged the urgency in a blog post announcing the changes.

"We have to continue to move fast with clear purpose here. We are committed to being at the frontier and are super focused on the areas where we need to improve."

— Sundar Pichai, Alphabet CEO

Alphabet shares fell 4% in midday trading after the announcement, erasing earlier gains. The stock reaction underscores investor anxiety about Google's standing in the AI race. Despite pioneering much of the underlying technology—including the transformer architecture that powers ChatGPT, Claude, and its own Gemini—Google has struggled to convert its research advantage into consistently superior commercial products.

What It Means for the AI Industry

The reorganization signals a broader maturation of the AI industry. Discovery Loop's structure as a public benefit corporation, focused on automating scientific discovery rather than building consumer AI, suggests that some of the field's most experienced engineers see opportunities outside the chatbot arms race.

For Google, the challenge is execution. Kavukcuoglu inherits a sprawling operation that spans fundamental research, product development across Search, Cloud, and consumer applications, and a computing infrastructure rivaling any in the world. Whether the structural change—flattening the reporting lines while elevating Hassabis to a strategic role—accelerates or slows Gemini's development will become clear in the months ahead.

What to Watch

The immediate test is Gemini 3.5 Pro. Every week it remains unreleased while Anthropic and OpenAI ship updates reinforces the perception that Google is losing ground. For the Indian tech workforce, which supplies a significant share of Google's AI engineering talent, the leadership reshuffle and talent drain add uncertainty to career calculations at one of the world's largest employers of Indian engineers.
nri_angle: The AI talent drain at Google raises questions for the large Indian engineering workforce at Alphabet, whose career trajectories are shaped by the company's competitive standing.
